YouTube channels and their analytics, and Google Business Profiles.

## Connect accounts

Each person connects their own YouTube account once, in the Gateway, and every app that asks for it uses that connection. Apps never see the tokens. [How connecting works](/docs/connect-oauth)

- **Make the OAuth app here:** [console.cloud.google.com](https://console.cloud.google.com/apis/credentials)
- **Settings:** `YOUTUBE_CLIENT_ID`, `YOUTUBE_CLIENT_SECRET`
- **Added with:** `everyapp provider add --oauth youtube`

### Redirect URI

Register this at the provider:

```text
https://<your gateway>/connect/youtube/callback
```

`<your gateway>` is your Gateway's address, like `apps.example.com`.

An app that runs the sign-in itself lists its own callbacks under `redirectPaths` in its manifest entry; register those too, as `https://<app>.<your gateway><path>`. `everyapp provider show youtube` prints every one.

### Make the OAuth app

Its own Google Cloud project, apart from google-workspace's: YouTube's scopes need their own verification. Not yet tried against a live connect.

1. Open [console.cloud.google.com](https://console.cloud.google.com/apis/credentials) and create an OAuth app (sometimes called a client or an integration).
2. Add the redirect URI above.
3. Allow the scopes behind the sets your apps use (the table below), and no others.
4. Copy the client ID and the client secret. The secret is often shown once.

Steps for this provider are brief. [Open an issue](https://github.com/every-app/every-app/issues/new?template=provider-request.yml&title=Provider%20guide%3A%20YouTube) to request a full guide.

### Set it on your Gateway

From your EveryApp folder:

```bash
everyapp provider add --oauth youtube
everyapp secret set YOUTUBE_CLIENT_ID YOUTUBE_CLIENT_SECRET
```

Each value goes in at a hidden prompt. Or, as an owner or admin, paste the client in **Manage workspace → Providers → Add OAuth provider**.

### Scope sets

Apps ask for named sets, never raw scopes, and the Gateway holds each app to the sets it declared.

| Set | Allows | Provider scopes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `identity` | Google account (who you are) | `https://www.googleapis.com/auth/userinfo.profile`, `https://www.googleapis.com/auth/userinfo.email` |
| `youtube.read` | YouTube channels and analytics (read) | `https://www.googleapis.com/auth/youtube.readonly`, `https://www.googleapis.com/auth/yt-analytics.readonly` |
| `youtube.write` | YouTube channels (upload and manage) | `https://www.googleapis.com/auth/youtube`, `https://www.googleapis.com/auth/youtube.upload`, `https://www.googleapis.com/auth/youtube.force-ssl` |
| `business.write` | Google Business Profiles (read and post) | `https://www.googleapis.com/auth/business.manage` |

### Use it in an app

```ts
capabilities: {
  youtube: { access: "read", scopes: ["youtube.read"], why: "What the app does with it." },
},
```

### Check it worked

- `everyapp provider show youtube` shows the client as set, and the redirect URI.
- Open the account menu → **Connected accounts** → **Connect YouTube**. You land back in the Gateway, connected.
- `everyapp provider connections` lists who has connected.
